findings: No policy-aware v1 export/import API on current main or latest stable.
Current-memory identity, file lookup, provenance and v1 save/load methods remain AST-identical to the tested 0.7.2 overlay.
Opaque export/install is planned rather than implemented. It does not itself solve ambient ownership.
Official RFC October18 update retracts the universal disjoint eager/graph bucket assumption; checked-in design non-goal text has not caught up.
Default process attachment and legacy file precedence are existing behavior; do not label that precedence an upstream bug without agreement.

decision.chosen_proposal: Optional v2 cache_scope=context managed-store peer; preserve current default process behavior and v1 eager path.
decision.alternative_not_chosen: Policy-aware v1 JSON export/import would extend the legacy persistence product; retain earlier manual proof as research only.
decision.not_authorized_for_production: Graph winners would use managed v2 persistence, relaxing the earlier proposal that both identities use v1 JSON. No SGLang production change or PR here.

limits: Concurrent tuning/serving remains unqualified because existing tuning counters are process-global.
No CUDA capture, native numerical or performance validation.
Current main is unreleased and does not include the separately qualified descriptor overlay.
Identified context tuning rejects shortlist ranking k>1.
Reload inside context scope is unsupported; outside it retains ambient-store semantics.
Calling discard helper in CPU controls does not qualify real distributed coordination.
